interface.title: EchoMetrics — Carcass Ultrasound Analyzer
interface.field: Animal science / meat science (carcass ultrasound evaluation)
interface.stage_of_work: Image measurement and data collection: taking measurements from images and exporting them as a table
interface.what_it_is_for: Measure the loin-eye (Longissimus dorsi) area and the subcutaneous fat thickness on B-mode carcass ultrasound images. You calibrate on the image's scale bar, trace an outline and mark two points, either one image at a time or as a coded batch exported to Excel.

data.note: The tool has no example image. The only test file was histology-he.jpg, a pink H&E histology picture rather than an ultrasound. It was uploaded 4 times, only to run through the workflow. Calibration points were placed arbitrarily, so the AOL and EGS numbers (2.79/0.5, 0.34/0.42, 1.77/0.5) mean nothing biologically. They are consistent with the pixel distances clicked, e.g. 100 px at 100 px/cm gave 1 cm, and 75 px at 150 px/cm gave 0.5 cm.

features.name: Two-point scale calibration on an image
features.general: Click the two ends of a known reference length on an image to set a pixels-per-unit scale, which then turns every later measurement into real units
features.specific: Step 1 — Calibrate (1 cm): click two points on the ultrasound scale bar; the Results panel shows 'Calibration: N px/cm', and AOL/EGS are converted with it
steps: Load an image; the calibration dialog opens on its own
Optionally zoom in or out with the magnifier buttons
Click the first end of the reference bar (yellow dot)
Click the second end; the scale is fixed and the dialog moves to the next step
serves_tasks: Set the image scale from a known length
Measure each image in the batch

features.name: Editable point-by-point outline for area
features.general: Draw a smoothed outline around a region by clicking control points, edit it (drag a point, undo the last one), then confirm to get the enclosed area in calibrated units; the curve is drawn open on screen, but the area is computed from the densely sampled smooth curve treated as closed
features.specific: Step 2 — Draw AOL: click points around the Longissimus dorsi, drag to adjust, right-click or Backspace to undo, then Enter or Confirm Shape; AOL appears in cm². No closing segment is drawn from the last point to the first
steps: Click points around the region; a green smoothed curve joins them, with a faint preview line to the cursor
Drag any point to move it (it turns red and the curve is redrawn)
Right-click or press Backspace to remove the last point
Press Enter or click Confirm Shape to finish; the area inside the curve, closed from last point back to first, is computed with the calibration
serves_tasks: Outline a region to measure its area
Measure each image in the batch

features.name: Two-point calibrated distance
features.general: Click two points across a layer to measure its thickness in real units
features.specific: Step 3 — Measure EGS: click two points across the subcutaneous fat; EGS appears in cm and the dialog closes
steps: Click the first edge of the layer (magenta dot)
Click the opposite edge; the distance is converted with the calibration and shown in Results
serves_tasks: Measure a layer's thickness between two points
Measure each image in the batch

features.name: Guided step-by-step measurement dialog with zoom
features.general: A dialog that leads the user through calibrate → outline → distance on one zoomable image canvas. Earlier marks stay visible, it can be cancelled, and results go to a side panel when it ends
features.specific: The dialog opens on upload and moves through 'Step 1 — Calibrate (1 cm)', 'Step 2 — Draw AOL' and 'Step 3 — Measure EGS', with zoom −/+ buttons (100%, 120%) and × to cancel. When it finishes, the Results panel fills in
steps: Upload an image to open the dialog at Step 1 (to reuse the same file, clear the file picker first; re-picking it directly does not reopen the dialog)
Zoom in or out with the buttons as needed (the mouse wheel does not zoom); clicks are corrected for zoom
Complete each step; the heading and instructions change and earlier marks stay on the image
After the last step the dialog closes and Results update, or press × to cancel without saving

features.name: Coded batch collection with spreadsheet export
features.general: Start a named batch, let each finished measurement become a row with an auto-numbered sample ID, watch the running count, and export all rows as a spreadsheet
features.specific: Batch mode: enter a Batch Code (LOTE01) and press Start Batch; each finished image is saved as LOTE0101, LOTE0102…; the info box shows 'N images saved'; Download Excel gives LOTE01_results.xlsx (per app.py: sheet 'Results', columns Image, AOL (cm²), EGS (cm), one row per sample); Reset ends the batch
steps: Type a batch code and press Start Batch (an empty code is refused with an error toast)
Measure images one by one; the count and next sample ID update after each
Press Download Excel (it appears after the first saved row) to get <code>_results.xlsx, a 'Results' sheet with Image, AOL (cm²) and EGS (cm) columns
Press Reset to clear the batch and return to Individual mode
serves_tasks: Measure each image in the batch
Export the accumulated batch results as a spreadsheet
